chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays al-Muradi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hawks and the falcons, and about their prey. He said: 'Eat what they have not killed, when you find it slaughtered. The end of slaughtering is when the eye twitches, the leg kicks, and the tail moves.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The hawks and the falcons are not mentioned in the Quran.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for eating prey caught by hawks and falcons according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic status of falcons and hawks by establishing that their prey is halal if consumed before death, defining the precise moment of slaughter (dhakat) through observable life signs like eye blinking and leg movement. The Imam’s note that these birds are not explicitly named in the Quran underscores the Shia method of deriving specific rulings from general principles (usul) and prophetic practice, rather than requiring explicit textual mention for every species.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Lays Al Murady who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the hawk and the falcon, and about its prey. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every prey which it did not kill when you came to it, so purify (slaughter) it, and the last of the purification (slaughtering) is when the eyes were fluttering and the legs were kicking and the tail was moving’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the hawk and the falcon are not in the Quran (to justify their killings)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ah al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Mufaddal ibn Salih from Layth al- Muradiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about falcons and hawks and their hunting. He (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever they have not killed and you have slaughtered properly, is lawful and the last time for slaughtering is when the eyes move, legs run and the tails move.’
He (the Imam) then said, ‘Hawks and falcons are not mentioned in the Quran.’”
